featured_reviews.name: Ashish Balachandran
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had one of the best experiences at Third Wave Coffee in Chowpatty, Girgaon. The highlight of this outlet is definitely the staff and their service.

👥 Service

The staff were extremely polite, prompt, and attentive. From taking the order to serving the drinks and food, everything was handled smoothly. The team was always available if we needed anything, and the service really made the experience pleasant.

🥤 Drinks
•	Strawberry Lemonade – Very refreshing with a good balance of sweetness and citrus. Perfect for a hot day.
•	Peach Bubble Tea – Quite enjoyable and flavourful. The peach taste was nice and the bubbles added a fun texture to the drink.

🍽️ Food
•	Bonanza Pizza – Slightly below average. The base and toppings were okay, but it didn’t really stand out compared to the drinks.
•	Chilli Cheese Toast – Absolutely fabulous. Crispy, cheesy, and perfectly balanced with just the right hint of chilli. Definitely one of the highlights of the meal.

🌿 Ambience

The ambience was fabulous. The café has a comfortable and relaxed vibe, making it a great place to sit, chat, or spend time with friends.

⭐ Final Verdict

While the Bonanza pizza could be improved, the drinks, chilli cheese toast, ambience, and especially the excellent service make this outlet stand out. Definitely one of the better Third Wave Coffee experiences in the Chowpatty–Girgaon area. ☕

featured_reviews.review_text:
Earth Café, Churchgate feels like a quiet pause button in the middle of Mumbai’s relentless rhythm. Tucked away yet perfectly placed, this café welcomes you with an earthy charm that instantly soothes the senses. The moment you step in, you’re greeted by a calming blend of natural tones, soft lighting, and a thoughtfully curated space that feels both modern and grounded—true to its name.

The ambience strikes a beautiful balance between cozy and classy, making it ideal for everything from relaxed conversations to peaceful solo time. Whether you’re catching up with a friend, working on your laptop, or simply enjoying a slow meal, Earth Café creates an atmosphere that encourages you to linger a little longer.

The food is where the café truly shines. Every dish feels fresh, wholesome, and crafted with care. From vibrant salads and nourishing bowls to indulgent yet guilt-free desserts, the menu caters wonderfully to health-conscious diners without compromising on taste. The beverages—especially their coffees and refreshing coolers—are well-balanced and thoughtfully prepared, making them perfect companions to the food.

What stands out most is the attention to detail: warm service, beautifully plated dishes, and a sense of calm that’s rare in the heart of South Mumbai. Earth Café isn’t just a place to eat; it’s an experience—one that leaves you feeling lighter, happier, and eager to return.

If South Mumbai’s cafe culture had to be summed up in one place, this would be it. Cafe Free India brings together great food, a lively setting, and an atmosphere that keeps you hooked from the moment you walk in.

The space carries a strong Goan inspired vibe, paired with an energy that feels vibrant and effortless. What truly sets it apart is the 📍Live Karaoke hosted Four Times a week ( Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, 9pm onwards ) It adds a sense of excitement to the entire experience and makes the place feel dynamic and interactive.

The food here leans towards indulgent comfort. The parmesan corn ribs are juicy and full of flavour, while the honey chilli lotus root stands out with the perfect balance of sweet and spice. Their pizzas are rich, cheesy, and consistently satisfying.

The drinks menu keeps things interesting with beers on tap and cocktails inspired by iconic parts of Mumbai like the Sea Link. Seasonal additions like the mango chilli margarita bring in a refreshing twist.

When it comes to desserts, this is where you should absolutely give in. The gooey brownie with vanilla ice cream paired with an irresistible mango cream is easily one of the highlights and something you cannot go wrong with.

Overall, Cafe Free India in Lower Parel delivers more than just a meal. With its food, drinks, and high energy karaoke nights, it is a place that promises a fun and memorable outing.

It is with considerable disappointment that I write regarding my visit to Starbucks, Churchgate, this afternoon.
I ordered two Grande Iced Brown Sugar Oatmilk , and I regret to say the drinks bore little resemblance to what they ought to be. Both were remarkably thin and watery, wholly lacking the body, richness, and balance one expects from this particular beverage. When I raised the matter with the server, I was told the drink was simply "low calorie." I explained that this did not account for how diluted it tasted, and requested something better prepared. Instead of helping, they simply said they “don’t know anything” and that the coupon was already entered into the system and expired, offering no explanation or solution.

This kind of careless handling and lack of accountability is unacceptable. The rude behavior, poor communication, and complete disregard for customer concerns made an already bad situation worse.

Truly a pathetic experience that completely ruined my day.

Cafe Markiv’s feels like a café that knows exactly what it wants to be and stays within that comfort zone. It offers a fairly extensive menu of continental and café-style dishes, presented neatly and priced in the mid-range for the area.

We tried the Americano, Peach Iced Tea, Grilled Chicken Risotto, and Chicken Markiv’s.

The Americano was straightforward and clean, no bitterness, no complexity. It does what an Americano is expected to do, without leaving a strong impression either way. The Peach Iced Tea was refreshing and mildly sweet, pleasant enough for Mumbai weather, though not particularly memorable.

The Chicken Risotto was decent. Creamy, adequately cooked, and comforting, but lacked depth or a distinct flavour punch. It felt safe rather than inspired. A good option if you’re in the mood for something mild and filling, but not something you’d crave or remember later.

The Chicken Markiv’s, which appears to be one of their signature dishes, was served well and plated nicely. The chicken was tender and paired with mashed potatoes and vegetables. Again, the flavours were balanced and acceptable, but it didn’t rise above being just fine. Nothing was wrong with the dish, but nothing truly stood out either.

The menu itself is broad, covering pizzas, burgers, pasta, risottos, rice plates, and main course options, both vegetarian and non-vegetarian. It caters well to mixed groups with varied preferences. Portions are reasonable, and pricing is what you’d expect from a café of this type.

Service was polite and timely, without being overly warm or inattentive. The ambience is comfortable and casual, suitable for conversations, short meetings, or a relaxed meal, though it doesn’t have a distinct character that sets it apart from similar cafés.

Overall, Cafe Markiv’s is reliable but unremarkable. Nothing great, nothing bad. It’s a decent place if you’re nearby and want a predictable café meal without surprises. Not a destination café, but functional and consistent for what it offers.
